title: Accelerator lifecycle Terraform module: ASG+Karpenter orchestration for private VPC
creator: Priya Ramesh
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that manages GPU accelerator node lifecycle in Private (VPC) deployments and orchestrates autoscaling across both ASG (Instance-based) and Karpenter (provisioner) paths. Module must handle mixed-instance types, spot/interruptible fallbacks, driver/OS upgrades, and provide healthcheck hooks for safe rolling upgrades.
background: Private deployments require tighter control over networking, IAM, and upgrade windows. Existing infra pieces are fragmented: ASG launch templates live in separate stacks, Karpenter provisioners are manually configured, and GPU driver upgrades are executed ad-hoc. Customer incidents during node driver/AMI upgrades demonstrated extended downtime when GPU pods are evicted and nodes fail to rejoin. We need a single Terraform module that codifies best practices for lifecycle (canary -> rolling) and integrates with our health and observability primitives.
design_notes:
High-level decisions:
- Single module exposing two modes: asg_mode and karpenter_mode. Only one active per deployment to avoid racing replacements.
- Support mixedInstancePolicy/instanceSelector to prefer on-demand but accept spot with fallback to on-demand pool.
- Integrate AWS Lifecycle Hooks for ASG to trigger pre-drain lambda that coordinates GPU operator safe-drain.
- For Karpenter, use provisioner taints and node-class annotations to ensure correct scheduling and graceful draining via node lifecycle controller.
- Driver upgrades are orchestrated via SSM Run Command and a scheduled upgrade plan; Terraform will manage SSM documents and maintenance window resources but not execute upgrades directly.
- Healthcheck agents post on startup to an internal health endpoint; failing nodes can be cordoned and SIGKILL after timeout.
- Metrics emitted to Console: node_boot_time, driver_install_status, graceful_drain_duration.
tasks: 1) Module scaffold: inputs/outputs, mode flag, VPC subnet/sg variables
2) ASG path: launch template with GPU AMI, user-data to install nvidia-driver, lifecycle hook + SNS topic + pre-drain lambda (lambda code in infra repo)
3) Karpenter path: provisioner CRD Terraform resource, instanceProfile/role attachments, taints/labels and node-template mapping
4) Mixed-instance & spot fallback: implement instance selector/mixedInstancePolicy with explicit on-demand fallback group
5) Healthchecks: bootstrap agent systemd unit + readiness probe registration in Console via API token secret
6) Driver upgrade orchestration: SSM Document + Maintenance Window resource + runbook link in module outputs
7) Canary workflow: create optional canary ASG/provisioner variable and helper script for canary rollout
8) Integration tests: terratest for module (ASG lifecycle simulation), k8s e2e for Karpenter path using aks-like cluster in CI
9) Documentation: usage examples for private VPC, variables reference, recommended upgrade cadence
10) Security review & IAM hardening: least-privilege roles for nodes, SSM and lifecycle hooks
acceptance_criteria: Module can be instantiated in a Private VPC to provision either an ASG-backed GPU pool or a Karpenter provisioner, controlled by input flag
Mixed instance/spot configuration is supported and provides an on-demand fallback pool when spot capacity is insufficient
Node lifecycle hooks coordinate pre-drain and post-terminate signals so GPU workloads are notified and drained within configured timeout
Driver upgrade documents and maintenance windows are created by Terraform; operator runbooks are linked from module outputs
Healthcheck agent registers node status and failures are surfaced to Console with runbook link; failing nodes are cordoned automatically after timeout
Module exposes outputs (launch_template_id / provisioner_name / iam_role_arn / maintenance_window_id) required by upstream stacks
Terratest CI passes for basic create/destroy + simulated lifecycle hook flow; basic k8s e2e for pod eviction and re-scheduling passes
